title: Thermal Stability and Phase Evolution in the Phosphorus-Containing High-Entropy Alloy Fe<sub>22</sub>Ni<sub>16</sub>Co<sub>19</sub>Mn<sub>12</sub>Cr<sub>16</sub>P<sub>15</sub>.

recollection.starting_material: Guess: an as-cast Fe22Ni16Co19Mn12Cr16P15 high-entropy alloy ingot made by arc melting and homogenized
recollection.intervention: Guess: systematic annealing / heat-treatment at 400-1000 °C combined with DSC, in-situ XRD and TEM to follow phase changes
recollection.structure: Guess: starts as a single-phase fcc solid solution that, on heating, precipitates nanometric phosphide phases (M3P, M2P) while retaining an fcc matrix; at still higher temperature an additional bcc phase may form
recollection.mechanism: Guess: phosphorus reduces solid-solution stability; during annealing P diffuses to defects and drives spinodal decomposition and heterogeneous nucleation of intermetallic phosphides, which strengthen the alloy until coarsening occurs
recollection.results: Guess: alloy stays single-phase up to about 650 °C. First exothermic event near 700 °C corresponds to ~10 vol % M3P precipitation, raising hardness from ~380 HV to ~540 HV and yield strength from ~950 MPa to ~1.3 GPa. Above ~900 °C a bcc phase appears and hardness drops to ~420 HV after prolonged exposure; grain size remains <2 µm after 10 h at 800 °C.

score.note: The recollection incorrectly substitutes an annealing and mechanical-strengthening study for the actual comparison of composition-modified arc-solidified and rapidly melt-spun material. It misses the eutectic multiphase ingot and fully amorphous ribbon, gives an unsupported spinodal/precipitation-strengthening mechanism, and reports fabricated temperatures, phase fractions, hardness, strength, and grain-size values. The nominal ~700 value is not creditable because it is stated in °C, whereas the actual event was near 699 K.
